paper_title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Segmenting a 3D object into semantically meaningful parts requires joint reasoning about geometric structure and semantic context. Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts. The challenge is to integrate these complementary capabilities into a framework that can both produce meaningful part segmentations and progressively refine them. We present PartAgent, a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation built upon two complementary modules: (i) Structural-Semantic Expert Integration combines regions predicted by the 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from the 2D expert through image-to-surface correspondences, constructing compositional part partitions at multiple granularities. (ii) Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement observes the current partition and its supporting evidence to select targeted inspection, evidence repair, composition, or reselection actions. It verifies proposed changes and uses the updated state and action outcomes to guide subsequent decisions. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT, PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU, outperforming the strongest competing method by 8.53 points. Across 3DCoMPaT200, PartNeXt, PartNetE, and PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartAgent achieves the highest mIoU on each dataset, averaging 69.36 across the four datasets, 7.28 points above the highest mean among competing methods.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Segmenting 3D object into semantically meaningful parts requires joint reasoning about geometric structure and semantic context. Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts. The challenge is to integrate these complementary capabilities into framework that can both produce meaningful part segmentations and progressively refine them. We present PartAgent, training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation (i) Structural built upon two complementary modules: *Corresponding author. Semantic Expert Integration combines regions predicted by the 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from the 2D expert through image-to-surface correspondences, constructing compositional part partitions at multiple granularities. (ii) Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement observes the current partition and its supporting evidence to select targeted inspection, evidence repair, composition, or reselection actions. It verifies proposed changes and uses the updated state and action outcomes to guide subsequent decisions. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT, PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU, outperforming the strongest competing method by 8.53 points. Across 3DCoMPaT200, PartNeXt, PartNetE, and PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartAgent achieves the 1 highest mIoU on each dataset, averaging 69.36 across the four datasets, 7.28 points above the highest mean among competing methods. 1. Introduction 3D part segmentation aims to partition 3D object into meaningful parts [9, 10, 2224, 46, 50], which is fundamental task in 3D understanding [4, 5, 25, 28, 29, 41]. Doing so requires both geometric cues about the objects structure and semantic context to determine which regions belong together. 3D experts [22, 23] propose spatially grounded regions, while image-based approaches [21, 36, 46] provide visual grouping and semantic context across views. Turning these complementary cues into meaningful parts remains challenging: (i) 3D proposal may cover only fragment of component or span several components, while semantic predictions from different views may disagree about part boundaries or identities. Constructing coherent partition therefore requires jointly considering geometric and semantic evidence to determine how regions should be grouped into parts. (ii) Even after integration, the initial partition may still be imperfect and require further inspection and revision. To address both challenges, we present PartAgent  (Fig. 2)  , training-free agentic framework that combines geometric and semantic evidence from pretrained 3D and 2D experts to construct meaningful part partitions, and then iteratively refines the segmentation by selecting targeted actions based on current observations. To construct meaningful initial partitions, our key intuition is to treat spatially grounded regions as building blocks and use semantic evidence to guide how they are refined and grouped into parts. We propose StructuralSemantic Expert Integration, which maps multiview semantic predictions onto the original mesh through image-to-surface correspondences and uses the mapped evidence to refine 3D expert regions. It then composes these regions into candidate partitions at multiple granularities, selects an initial partition, and retains alternative candidates for later revision. Further refinement requires deciding where to inspect, what to revise, and whether proposed change improves the result. We propose Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement, which uses visionlanguage model (VLM) to examine projected partitions, geometry renders, and semantic predictions and select targeted action. The agent can inspect region, repair 2D segmentation masks, revise part groupings, or select an alternative candidate. The agent verifies each proposed update before adoption. Both acceptance and rejection guide later actions. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT [23], PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU, outperforming the strongest competing method by 8.53 points. Across 3DCoMPaT200 [1], PartNeXt [39], PartNetE [21], and PartObjaverse-Tiny [46], PartAgent Figure 2. From 3D expert to an agentic framework. (a) 3D expert directly segments the object into parts. (b) PartAgent integrates predictions from frozen 2D and 3D experts and iteratively refines the segmentation through an observation-driven loop. achieves the highest mIoU on each dataset, with fourdataset mean of 69.36, exceeding the strongest competing methods mean by 7.28 points. Fig. 1 shows PartAgent segmenting diverse, complex 3D assets drawn from existing benchmarks or generated with Hunyuan3D [16] into parts. Our contributions are threefold: Training-Free Agentic Framework for 3D Part Segmentation. We integrate frozen 2D and 3D experts to construct meaningful part partitions and iteratively refine them through VLM-guided decisions. StructuralSemantic Expert Integration. We use multiview semantic evidence to refine 3D expert regions and compose candidate partitions at multiple granularities. Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement. We introduce an observation-driven loop that adaptively refines both part groupings and their supporting semantic evidence. Verification determines which updates to adopt and provides feedback for subsequent action selection. 2. Related Work 3D part representations and segmentation. Point and mesh networks encode geometry using dynamic graphs [40], mesh-edge convolutions [13], and attention [43, 49]. PartNet [25] provides hierarchical part annotations. PartField [22] clusters part-aware features, while P3-SAM [23] predicts native 3D masks with automatic selection and merging. PartSAM [50] uses native 3D supervision for scalable, promptable part segmentation. SegviGen [19] adapts native 3D generative model to color-code object parts. PartGen [8] combines multiview part segmentation and completion with 3D reconstruction. PartAgent builds candidate segmentations from 2D and 3D predictions and chooses refinement actions based on what it observes. Multiview transfer for 3D segmentation. Transformers and self-supervised learning [7, 11, 38] enable pretrained models to extract visual features and interpret images [2, 3, 18, 20, 26, 31, 45]. Promptable models generate 2 Figure 3. Overview of PartAgent. (A) StructuralSemantic Expert Integration (SSEI) uses multiview semantic evidence to refine 3D expert regions and combine them into candidate segmentations at multiple granularities, then selects an initial segmentation P0. (B) Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement (CLR) uses VLM to examine the current segmentation and its supporting evidence and choose targeted actions. Proposed segmentation updates are verified before adoption, and feedback guides subsequent actions. segmentation masks [6, 14]. PartSLIP [21] lifts languageguided detections to point clouds. SAMesh [36] links masks across mesh views, while SAMPart3D [46] distills scale-conditioned features using multiview semantic labels. S2AM3D [33] combines 2D priors and 3D supervision for consistent features and controllable segmentation granularity. For scenes, OpenScene [27] and OpenMask3D [35] transfer language-aligned features to points and instance masks, respectively. SAMPro3D [44] uses shared 3D prompts across views. PartAgents SSEI uses multiview semantics to refine and group 3D expert regions, then selects one complete segmentation and retains alternatives for later revision. Agentic perception and refinement. Agentic methods act on intermediate observations [15, 37]. ReAct [47] interleaves reasoning and action, and Reflexion [32] retains feedback without updating weights. Visual Programming [12] and ViperGPT [34] compose pretrained modules into executable programs. VASA [42] inspects and edits masks for open ad-hoc 2D segmentation. Agent3D-Zero [48] selects viewpoints for 3D understanding. A3R [17] learns to gather evidence sequentially for instruction-conditioned affordance grounding in Gaussian scenes. For 3D part segmentation, PartAgent uses observations and verification feedback to repair multiview 2D masks, regroup 3D regions, or choose another complete segmentation from its candidates. 3. We evaluate all 200 objects in each of the PartObjaverse-Tiny [46] and PartObjaverse-TinyWT [23] benchmarks. To keep API costs manageable on the larger PartNeXt [39], 3DCoMPaT200 [1], and PartNetE [21] benchmarks, we select 500 objects per dataset through category-balanced random sampling. We evaluate all methods on the same fixed subsets using their officially released code and pretrained models. For the same reason, all ablations use the same fixed set of 100 meshes randomly sampled from PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT. We will release all the evaluation data and splits. Following PartField [22], our main comparisons report Mask Match mIoU. For each object, we match each ground-truth part mask to the predicted candidate mask with the highest IoU and average these IoUs. For each object, we average scores within each annotation level, then across the available levels. Dataset scores average these object scores. Avg. in Tab. 2 is the mean of the four datasetlevel scores. For ablations, we also report Partition Match mIoU. Mask Match evaluates individual part masks, while Partition Match evaluates complete candidate partitions. Models and inference. We use frozen P3-SAM [23] as the 3D expert and GPT-Image-2.5 as the 2D expert for image segmentation and repair. We use gpt-6.1-sol for reasoning and verification. We render each object from four fixed viewpoints. For PartNetE point clouds, we use point neighborhoods and pixelpoint correspondences in place of mesh adjacency and pixelface mappings. In each controlled comparison, we change only the tested component and keep all other settings fixed. For each object, CLR action and VLM comparisons share the initial segmentation, candidate partitions, and multiview evidence from SSEI. 4.2. Comparison with Previous Methods Watertight meshes. As shown in Tab. 1, PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU on PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT, outperforming the strongest competing method (59.88) by 8.53 points. PartAgent also ranks first in all eight object categories. The largest margins over the best competing score in each category are 11.15 points for transportation, 10.04 for plants, and 9.43 for human models. All methods use the same matching procedure to compare their predicted candidate masks with the ground-truth part masks for each object. Multiple benchmarks. Tab. 2 reports mIoU averaged over objects for each dataset. PartAgent achieves the highest mIoU on all four datasets, with 67.82 on 3DCoMPaT200, 72.42 on PartNeXt, 71.43 on PartNetE, and 65.76 on PartObjaverse-Tiny. Its mean mIoU across the four datasets is 69.36, exceeding the highest mean among competing methods (62.08) by 7.28 points. Qualitative comparison. Fig. 6 compares PartAgent with competing methods. Across the tested 2D experts and refinement VLMs, PartAgent outperforms P3-SAM alone on both Partition Match and Mask Match mIoU (Tab. 5). These results show that PartAgent remains effective with different models for 2D mask generation and CLR. Performance across refinement loops. Fig. 7 shows how Mask Match mIoU changes as refinement proceeds. After each loop, we evaluate the candidates generated so far. mIoU increases from 67.60 at initialization to 68.94 after Loop 6. As the agent inspects and revises the segmentation over successive loops, the candidate segmentations achieve higher mIoU. This supports our intuition that PartAgent can progressively improve segmentation by refinement. Qualitative loop evolution. Fig. 5 shows how the segmentation changes over successive refinement loops. In Loop 1, the agent groups the cable and its connector into one part, while the control panel remains fragmented. In Loop 2, the agent examines the updated segmentation and merges fragments within the enclosure and within the control panel, while keeping the cable, handpiece, and holder separate. sections.title: Supplemental Material
sections.content: To limit API costs, we conduct the ablations in the main paper on 100 randomly sampled meshes from PartObjaverse-TinyWT [23]. Here we repeat the ablations of our core modules, SSEI and CLR, on the remaining 100 meshes to see whether the same findings hold. As shown in Tab. S1, adding SSEI to the 3D expert improves Partition Match and Mask Match on both sets. Adding CLR on top of SSEI improves both metrics further. The improvements show that our findings also hold on the remaining objects. Table S1. Ablations of PartAgents core modules (SSEI and CLR) on PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT. Partition and Mask denote Partition Match and Mask Match mIoU (%, ). Original 100 Remaining 100 Variant Partition 3D Expert only 3D Expert + CLR SSEI only Full PartAgent 58.51 62.72 65.11 65.98 Mask 58.51 64.37 67.60 68.94 Partition 58.84 62.56 63.73 64. Mask 58.84 63.66 66.77 67.88 B. More Qualitative Comparisons Fig. S1 and Fig. S2 show examples comparing PartAgent with the competitive methods, i.e., SAMPart3D [46], PartField [22], P3-SAM [23], and PartSAM [50]. Colors distinguish predicted parts. 11 Figure S1. Qualitative comparisons (1/2). PartAgent reduces fragmentation on continuous surfaces while keeping adjacent parts separate. 12 Figure S2. Qualitative comparisons (2/2). PartAgent reduces fragmentation on continuous surfaces while keeping adjacent parts separate. 13 C. Additional Ablation Analyses C.1. Qualitative Loop Evolution Fig. S3 and Fig. S4 show examples of refinement. Loop 0 denotes the SSEI initialization, and later numbers denote the loop rounds. The insets use the same camera, location, and magnification at each loop. Figure S3. Qualitative closed-loop evolution (1/2). Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement progressively improves part segmentation over multiple loops. 14 Figure S4. Qualitative closed-loop evolution (2/2). Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement progressively improves part segmentation over multiple loops. 15 C.2. CLR Action Ablations We further ablate Compose, Repair 2D, and Reselect to examine how these actions contribute to closed-loop refinement. As shown in Tab. S2, removing Compose lowers Partition and Mask by 0.86 and 1.16 points, respectively. Removing Reselect lowers them by 0.25 and 0.29 points. And removing Repair 2D lowers them by 0.02 and 0.09 points. Repair 2D yields small average gains but helps prevent an occasional failure that matters in practice. When the 2D expert hallucinates part, the incorrect mask can introduce false part into the 3D segmentation. Fig. S5 provides qualitative examples of how repairing the 2D masks removes false regions and corrects misplaced boundaries in the 3D segmentation. This matters in practice when part hallucinated by the 2D expert would otherwise appear as separate part in the final result. Table S2. Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement. All variants start from the same SSEI initialization and use the Original 100 meshes in Tab. S1. Partition and Mask report Partition Match and Mask Match mIoU (%, ), respectively. Compose Repair 2D Reselect Partition 65.12 65.96 65. 65.98 Mask 67.78 68.85 68.65 68.94 Figure S5. Repair 2D examples. Each row shows the same cropped view before and after repair. Repair 2D removes hallucinated regions and corrects other errors in the 2D experts masks, improving the corresponding 3D segmentation.
